issues.message: Fish and kelp use the same generic head/status UI; product identity must be conveyed by distinct product icon, silhouette, color and count treatment.
issues.evidence: fish/kelp stock states in screenshot set

issues.message: Upgrade availability is not stage-gated with a dedicated visual unlock state; locked, available and maxed progression need distinct icon UI.
issues.evidence: upgrade examples show icon+price progression and locked/available distinction

issues.message: Payment/investment lacks a visible coin-to-node transaction animation and construction completion transition.
issues.evidence: currency stack and completed-device examples in screenshot set

issues.message: After construction completes, the new device/source must appear as a persistent functional visual object, not only a changed number or label.
issues.evidence: completed device state example contrasted with current tide-pool presentation

reproductionMatrix.rendererPresentationPath: world source renderer and state badge

acceptanceCriteria: Fish and kelp carried/shelf cues use distinct product icons and visual treatments; no generic shared head badge is used for both.
Upgrade UI has visually distinct locked, stage-eligible, purchasable, purchased and maxed states; availability is driven by progression state, not explanatory prose.
Investment visibly animates shell coins into the node, shows partial progress, and on threshold completion transitions the node into a persistent active device visual.
The completed device remains visible and functional after refresh and the next natural interaction uses the same world object.
Add RED tests before implementation, then run GREEN, build, exact natural-input traces and perceptual QA for every matrix cell.
